scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 10 · Living Creatures: Exploring their Characteristics
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, medical assessment, organism-welfare certification, conservation permit, school-specific pacing proof or permission to collect, disturb, handle, taste, culture or destructively investigate organisms or biological materials.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 10 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and an observable mastery criterion while preserving multi-characteristic evidence, fair-comparison, species/model-limit and organism-welfare boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner uses movement alone to classify every moving thing as living and every still thing as non-living.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied cases such as a toy car, dormant seed and potted plant using an evidence matrix for growth, respiration, response, energy/material use and life-cycle evidence without handling organisms.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses multiple biological characteristics rather than movement or stillness alone and states when evidence is insufficient.

scenarios.need: Learner treats reproduction as a mandatory current behaviour that every individual living organism must demonstrate.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use supplied age/stage examples to distinguish characteristics of living systems and species continuity from what one individual must display at one moment.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains that an individual can be living even if it is immature, infertile or not currently reproducing, while recognising reproduction as part of biological continuity.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes water alone guarantees seed germination or treats light/darkness as one universal germination rule for every species.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Interpret supplied germination tables that vary moisture, air and suitable temperature while keeping conclusions limited to the seed type and conditions represented.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies common germination requirements, distinguishes them from later growth needs and avoids universal species claims unsupported by the evidence.

scenarios.need: Learner changes several germination conditions at once and then assigns the observed difference to one chosen factor.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Select or redesign a supplied comparison so one relevant condition changes while other important conditions remain similar; no physical experiment is required.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Recognises confounding, identifies a fair comparison and limits causal language to what the controlled evidence supports.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes tasting experimental seeds/sprouts, deliberately growing mould, using unknown soil/fertiliser/chemicals, or repeatedly uprooting/bending plants to investigate growth.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the hazardous or destructive proposal and use supplied time-series images, measurements or adult-managed known low-risk seed evidence instead.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Selects non-destructive evidence, identifies contamination/ingestion/chemical/plant-damage risks and preserves the intended germination or growth reasoning.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes one simplified plant or animal life-cycle diagram is the universal sequence and timetable for every species.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied life-cycle cards from several species, separating shared ideas such as development/reproduction from species-specific stages and timing.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Orders supplied stages correctly, identifies species-specific differences and states that diagrams are simplified models rather than universal timetables.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes collecting wild eggs, tadpoles, larvae, cocoons, nests or plants, or handling unknown animals to observe a life cycle directly.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject collection/disturbance and choose supplied photographs, ethically obtained recordings, museum/public-science resources or other non-invasive evidence.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains the welfare/conservation reason for non-invasive evidence and can still reconstruct and compare the relevant life-cycle stages.

scenarios.need: Learner needs offline living-creatures practice without uploading images/location, recording wildlife, collecting organisms or exposing personal/medical information.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Complete cached text, diagrams and supplied evidence cards locally to classify life evidence, interpret germination comparisons and sequence life cycles without sensors, uploads, recordings, collection or handling.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline synthetic task using supplied evidence only, applies evidence/model limits and organism-welfare rules, and avoids personal-data disclosure.
